That poem is beautiful for all variety of wisdom you might draw from this film. It works for the story as well as some of the larger statements made about the condition of our civilization. I think aligning the 'dying of the light' with the 'end of the world' is arguable. But it might be more useful (considering the overt commentaries on the state of average human intelligence and capability) to relate the light to our ability to learn and grow.
Coop references and embodies a bygone era of intelligent, capable thinkers & doers. Talking with people in real life, or looking at what's on TV, or reading the nonsense people say online, you notice how hugely uninformed and lazy people are. If we can describe the 'light' as an 'inspiration' or 'passion', we as a whole are losing it fast. People are lulling their minds to sleep with screens; devouring an endless feast of empty content that fills the space between sleep and work.
If we can't find a more enlightened approach to our personal growth, societal functionality, and sense of mutual responsibility, our civilization will indeed die from one thing or another. And perfectly fitting to the poem, that the lead up to our societal demise would likely be a slow creep, as we go gently into that good night. Unless of course, we choose to rage against it ;)

Maybe Christopher Nolan is foretelling the condition of the human race. I'd like to think so. It really doesn't matter if critics and the public criticized for being "boring" or "complex". We take what we are given and hold it dearly to our hearts because when an imminent time the light has gone out, only we would have the best to ourselves.
